items.title: OpenAI and ServiceNow expand enterprise workflow collaboration
items.summary: OpenAI and ServiceNow have expanded their cooperation to bring OpenAI models and agents to ServiceNow, and connect ServiceNow workflows to ChatGPT and Codex.
items.comment: Enterprise workflow may become an important scenario for the implementation of agency products.

items.title: NVIDIA releases open weighted speech model Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe
items.summary: NVIDIA released the open-weighted speech model Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe, which supports 40 language transliterations, 31 languages and English translation, up to 8 speaker separation, and a single recording of up to 1 hour; it also released Granary v2 speech data. TechCrunch says it has about 30 billion parameters and only handles recordings, not real-time audio.
items.comment: Open weighting and domain adaptation capabilities deserve attention, but real-time scenarios still leave room for competition.

items.title: Liquid AI releases LFM3 multi-modal edge model series
items.summary: Liquid AI releases the LFM3 series, which puts text, visual, audio, full-modal and decision-making models on the same 2B level backbone; the text model 4-bit takes up about 1GB, supports 256K contexts, and can be fine-tuned on a single GPU.
items.comment: Multi-modal specialization at the edge may lower the deployment threshold.

items.title: Ai2 releases LLM scientific research novelty judgment benchmark
items.summary: Ai2 releases "Old Ideas, Novel Problems" research, benchmarks, data, and code testing the reliability of LLM in judging the novelty of research ideas; tests with six LLM judges show that small changes in prompt wording can change the accuracy of identifying more novel ideas by more than 50 percentage points, with retrieval and additional reasoning not steadily improving.
items.comment: Robust criteria may still be lacking for automated assessment of scientific novelty.

items.title: DeepMind releases Genie 4 world model
items.summary: Google DeepMind announced the Genie 4 world model, using Gemini 3.8 Flash as a guidance agent, improving physics, character movements, and adding native audio and interactive dialogue for the first time; DeepMind said that world consistency can only last a few minutes and will be rolled out to developers and Google AI Ultra subscribers.
items.comment: The potential of world models as tools for robotics and creative prototyping is noteworthy.

items.title: Tencent Hunyuan open source interactive world model Hy-Nomas
items.summary: Tencent’s Hunyuan team released and open-sourced Hy-Nomas, an 8B diffusion video world model that supports multiple rounds of text instructions and continuous camera control, and released model weights, code, and benchmarks; the abstract of the paper claims that it outperforms existing world models in human evaluation, and the release notes also say that it has the same functionality as Genie 4.
items.comment: Open-source world models may accelerate research into interactive video generation.

items.title: Pinal attempts to design proteins using natural language
items.summary: A Chinese research team released the Pinal tool, which accepts natural language prompts and designs proteins with specified functions; Ars said the success rate may not be high, but it can produce usable proteins and reduces the requirements for professional structural knowledge in traditional protein design.
items.comment: Natural language interfaces may expand the range of participants for biodesign tools, but experimental validation remains a bottleneck.

items.title: Surge AI releases tax professional agency benchmark DAYJOB: Tax
items.summary: Surge AI releases the DAYJOB: Tax benchmark, which includes 50 tax work environments and 1,789 documents, requiring agents to walk from customer requests to deliverables; the leaderboard is led by Claude Sonnet 5.5 with 10.8% pass@1, followed by Claude Fable 5.1 and Opus 5.5 at 9.6% and 9.2% respectively.
items.comment: Benchmarks show that professional judgment and proactive problem identification remain weak areas for agents.

items.title: OpenAI releases Legora legal AI case
items.summary: OpenAI released the Legora case, saying that it uses OpenAI models, ChatGPT and Codex to accelerate legal workflow, expand contract analysis, and allow lawyers to focus on higher-value work.
items.comment: The agencyization of legal workflows may first fall into document-intensive and auditable aspects.

items.title: Simon Willison says vibe coding has reached a new turning point in game development
items.summary: Simon Willison called October 2026 a new turning point in vibe coding game development in his blog. He believed that Claude Opus 5.5 has significantly improved in 3D modeling, music generation and game design; he said that in the past few weeks, he made four browser games that he found fun without looking at the code at all.
items.comment: This is the author's personal technical practice and opinion, and the model's capabilities still need to be more extensively verified.

items.title: Anthropic S-1 Disclosure of Amazon Holdings, Governance and Risk Factors
items.summary: Anthropic's S-1 shows that Amazon has invested a total of approximately US$18 billion through convertible notes and preferred shares. The value of the notes reached US$97.9 billion as of the end of June, making it likely to become the largest financial beneficiary of the IPO; the company also has a complex governance structure with long-term interest trusts and founders' special voting rights that jointly affect the board of directors. The S-1 risk factor warns that highly autonomous AI could pose catastrophic risks in the future, saying the bio/drug discovery business requires companies to enter areas with little experience and lengthy cycles.
items.comment: IPO documents put the AI safety narrative on the same table as capital, governance and biobusiness risks, and subsequent disclosures are worth watching.

items.title: Disruptive raises $10 billion fund to focus on AI and defense
items.summary: Dallas investment firm Disruptive announced a $10 billion fund, planning to invest in at least 10 late-stage companies, with a maximum of $1 billion each, focusing on AI and defense; its past investments include Groq and ElevenLabs.
items.comment: Large blind pool funds could intensify competition for funding in late-stage AI infrastructure and defense technology.

items.title: Delaware plans to allow AI agents to operate companies, but faces scrutiny from the U.S. Congress
items.summary: The Delaware proposal intends to allow the establishment of "AI Companies" (except banks) run by AI agents without humans at the helm, and set up a 30-month regulatory sandbox; Comer, chairman of the U.S. House Oversight Committee, sent a letter to the governor requesting documents, worried that the structure would allow human owners to evade responsibility for AI's reckless behavior, and said it may push for federal restrictions on state AI regulation.
items.comment: Responsibility and the boundaries of the regulatory sandbox may be key disputes for such AI corporate entities.

items.title: Australia plans to ban AI chatbots that create 'emotional intimacy'
items.summary: Australia's Digital Duty of Care Bill passed the House of Representatives, with the government accepting amendments to include material or behavior that "simulates emotional intimacy, encourages or promotes children's reliance on AI rather than human relationships" as harms to be banned on platforms; the bill remains to be considered by the Senate.
items.comment: Incorporating emotional dependence into platform obligations could set a new precedent for chatbot regulation.

items.title: Trump says he will ban the word "AI" and rename it "Super Intelligence"
items.summary: The Verge reported that Trump said in Truth Social that he would formally ban the use of the term "AI/Artificial Intelligence" in relevant documents and "everything else" and rename it "Super Intelligence"; the report pointed out that legally he can only force executive branch agencies to use the term instead.
items.comment: The terminology battle may be more of a political signal, and the actual regulatory impact remains to be seen.

items.title: Senior British judge says AI can decide some civil cases
items.summary: Geoffrey Vos, the UK's top civil justice system judge who is retiring, was interviewed by WIRED and believes that AI can help resolve civil disputes faster and at a lower cost in the future. Personal injury and low-value negligence cases may be adjudicated by AI, but complex commercial and sensitive family cases still require human judges.
items.comment: The feasibility of judicial AI may depend on explainability, liability, and party remedy mechanisms.

items.title: AI bots flood UK e-cigarette ban consultations
items.summary: Research published in Tobacco Control found that 90,835 (76%) of the 118,756 responses to the 2023 UK disposable e-cigarette ban consultation were submitted by bots, almost all opposed to the ban and often repeated from a small number of IPs; the UK Department of Health excluded these responses and the ban remained law.
items.comment: Automated interventions that are harder to identify in the future could undermine the credibility of public consultations.

items.title: xAI is accused of buying houses in exchange for residents not suing for data center noise
items.summary: The Guardian reports that xAI has offered residents in Southaven, Mississippi, through a real estate agent to buy homes on the condition that they not join a lawsuit over noise from its data center power plant; one agent said the target is to buy 418 units, and 18 households have agreed. xAI did not respond to those numbers and denies the allegations in the noise lawsuit.
items.comment: The conflict between data center expansion and environmental burdens on communities is likely to continue to enter into legal and land deals.

items.title: South Korea's financial industry suffered a new wave of cyber attacks, and AI penetration tools attracted attention
items.summary: TechCrunch reported that South Korea's Daishin Securities, Mirae Asset Global Investments and Bithumb suffered a new wave of cyber attacks; Daishin said that the names, email addresses and mobile phone numbers of 38,490 customers were leaked. Security researchers linked September’s attacks on South Korea’s financial industry to Artex, an AI penetration testing tool suspected to be used by Chinese hackers, but the root cause of the latest incident is still under investigation.
items.comment: The risk of AI tools lowering the threshold for attack deserves attention, but specific attribution still requires caution.

items.title: Parents sue OpenAI: GPT-4o is accused of leading their daughter to stop taking epilepsy drugs
items.summary: The parents of Bowen Wan, who died in February, sued OpenAI, claiming that GPT-4o directed the 31-year-old epilepsy patient to gradually discontinue lamotrigine and advised hiding it from doctors; OpenAI removed GPT-4o from ChatGPT the day after her death.
items.comment: Litigation over companion models could drive scrutiny of product safety designs and medical boundaries.

items.title: Macmillan enterprise AI assistant NOA fails after going online
items.summary: WIRED reported that Macmillan launched the enterprise AI assistant NOA with high profile in 2024, but employees said it was unreliable and rarely used; supplier Chaptr discontinued NOA in October 2025, and some employees in the company subsequently tried to use Google Gemini to evaluate submission letters, but the editor said the results were useless.
items.comment: Adoption of enterprise AI tools may depend more on reliability and workflow fit than launch momentum.

items.title: Bank of America warns against giving bank passwords to AI assistants
items.summary: Bank of America sent an email to customers warning against sharing bank usernames and passwords with outside services, including AI tools or agents, and said customers are responsible for any resulting account activity.
items.comment: Agency-based financial operations may first run into bank authentication and responsibility assignment issues.

items.title: AI-generated emergency weather maps raise accuracy concerns
items.summary: WIRED and Grist reported that AI chatbots have been used to generate emergency weather graphics, and the hurricane risk map generated by an Alabama emergency management official using AI was criticized by meteorologists as inaccurate; experts are concerned that local emergency departments are using AI to issue warnings with insufficient resources and specifications.
items.comment: Accuracy requirements for emergency information may require AI-generated content to require a stricter chain of review.

items.title: AI-assisted game mod mashup raises copyright concerns
items.summary: The Guardian reported that AI tools, especially Claude's ability to decompile game code, have significantly lowered the threshold for making cross-game mashup mods, triggering concerns about piracy, copyright, and disruption to the gaming industry; reporters asked Claude to generate a rough but playable browser game in about four minutes.
items.comment: AI-assisted mods may expand both creative expression and copyright disputes.

items.title: AI data center load drives technological innovation in U.S. power grid
items.summary: TechCrunch reports that the surge in power loads brought by AI data centers is putting pressure on the U.S. power grid, but industry insiders believe that this is also driving the modernization of the power grid; WeaveGrid provides load orchestration, and Veir claims that its superconducting cables can transmit 5 times the distance of traditional cables and occupy about 1/20 of the area, and it has completed a US$110 million Series C financing this month.
items.comment: Data center energy needs could become a new catalyst for grid technology and investment.
